entities.summary: Sir Denys Tudor Emil Roberts was a British colonial official and judge. Joining the colonial civil service as a Crown Counsel in Nyasaland in 1953, he became Attorney General of Gibraltar in 1960. In 1962, he was posted to Hong Kong as Solicitor-General, and was successively promoted to Attorney-General in 1966, Colonial Secretary/Chief Secretary in 1973 and Chief Justice in 1979. He was the first and only Attorney-General to become both Colonial Secretary in Hong Kong. Never having been a judge before, he was appointed as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court in 1979 and was the first and only Colonial Secretary of Hong Kong to receive such appointment.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Attorney-General of Hong Kong and Colonial Secretary, Denys Roberts played a crucial role in shaping the territory's legal framework and governance. His appointment as Chief Justice marked a significant milestone in Hong Kong's judicial system.
